retrievals.source_citation: Kirsty Rowan, 'Revising the Sound Value of Meroitic D: A Phonological Approach', Beitrage zur Sudanforschung 10 (2009), SOAS eprint 12838 (open access; copy retrieved via Internet Archive Wayback Machine because the live host failed DNS)
retrievals.source_locator: PDF page 7 of 8 (text line 335 table '(10)', text lines 340-342 the /kandake/ sentence); extracted text /tmp/r8f15/rowan2009.txt; PDF copy /tmp/r8f15/rowan2009.pdf
source_excerpts: There is an orthographic practice in Meroitic whereby a nasal segment in coda position followed by a consonant is unwritten. Therefore the Meroitic form ekdk kdke is phonemically /kandake/
Meroitic ekdk (ektk) kdke (ktke) title; Egyptian kntiky; Greek κανδάκη; Ethiopic xan(ə)dākē
retrievals.retrieval_method: curl -sS -L of the Wayback Machine capture (HTTP 200; live eprints.soas.ac.uk attempt failed DNS, see access_failures), then pdftotext -layout extraction
retrievals.support_scope: passage-level: directly supports the entry's line 82 mechanism (written form lacks visible n; nasal recovered from equivalents) and the entry's table rows that treat kdke as a title whose Greek/Latin forms are transmission, not reconstruction.
retrievals.notes: This is the first peer-reviewed passage retrieved for the title-translation leg; it does not verify Hofmann 1981 p. 41 or Torok 1997 pp. 213-214, which remain unread (documented failures below). Rowan argues the nasal is phonemically present in /kandake/; the entry's claim that a bare kdke spelling is 'not sufficient to pronounce the title without a nasal' is consistent with, and mechanically explained by, this passage.

basis: Fresh round-8 live retrieval on 2026-10-17 re-fetched the entry's own cited Strabo witness (HTTP 200, sha256 ab1fa7fa…, line-located quotes) and re-confirmed every item the entry's line 85 asserts: a ruling woman, her generals captured, her son at Napata, ambassadors offering captives and statues, and the attributed gendered description (line 86). The title-translation leg, tertiary-only in round 6, now has a peer-reviewed passage (Rowan 2009, open access) stating that the Meroitic written form kdke is phonemically /kandake/ because a coda nasal is unwritten — the mechanism behind the entry's line 82 caveat — and printing the Egyptian/Greek/Ethiopic equivalence chain. Queen/queen-mother contextualization is freshly retrieved but only at tertiary grade, with the entry's anchored page range (Torok 1997 pp. 213-214) confirmed as a citation in the fresh fetch. The prior transcription doubt is settled at the digital-witness level: the singular 'fugitive' is what the cited witness reads.
limits: Whole-claim support stays partial: (1) Hofmann 1981 p. 41 and Torok 1997 pp. 213-214 remain unread (documented failures, lending-restricted or absent from accessible indexes); (2) the queen-mother contextualization rests on tertiary mediation; (3) the Greek original text was not retrieved (Perseus 503), so κανδάκη is evidenced only as printed in the Rowan table and the Wikipedia footnote; (4) no object/inscription witness (e.g. a Meroitic royal inscription using kdke) was retrieved, so the title's epigraphic attestation remains pointer-level; (5) the printed Loeb page was not imaged, so print-level typography of 'fugitive' remains unverified; (6) individual ruler identification and royal imagery were not re-retrieved in this shard. Nothing in this receipt evidences or refutes a universal gender system.
